name: Rain of Riches
oracle_text:
When this enchantment enters, create two Treasure tokens.
The first spell you cast each turn that mana from a Treasure was spent to cast has cascade. (When you cast the spell, exile cards from the top of your library until you exile a nonland card that costs less. You may cast it without paying its mana cost. Put the exiled cards on the bottom in a random order.)
blocked_sentences: The first spell you cast each turn that mana from a Treasure was spent to cast has cascade.

needs.what: a spell_cast trigger `nth: 1` whose filter includes `paid_by: {"subtypes": ["Treasure"]}`, counting this turn's earlier spells by whether Treasure mana paid for them: keep each spell's `mana_spent_traits` in the turn ledger (by cast id) and let `_spell_ordinal` match `paid_by` against them, so the ordinal counts only Treasure-paid spells. Then the line can be written as a triggered ability `{event: spell_cast, controller: you, nth: 1, filter: {paid_by: {subtypes: [Treasure]}}}` with effects `[{op: cascade, max_mana_value: {mana_value_of: {objects: {binding: subject}}}}]` (or as a real 'spell gains cascade' grant)
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `nth` on a filtered spell_cast trigger counts earlier spells through `_spell_ordinal`, which matches only printed characteristics (ORDINAL_FILTER_KEYS), and the loader refuses `paid_by` beside `nth`. `max_per_turn: 1` is the near miss and is wrong: it caps this permanent's firings rather than asking whether the spell is the turn's first Treasure-paid spell, so if Rain of Riches is itself cast with Treasure mana (or arrives after a Treasure-paid spell), the next Treasure-paid spell that turn would wrongly cascade. Cascade is also not a grantable keyword in `keywords`, so 'has cascade' can only be approximated by a trigger from this enchantment.

closest_existing: spell_cast trigger with paid_by filter (Treasure class: 'if mana from a Treasure was spent to cast it')
